finding.summary: Reviewed four weeks of digests and tagged every entry that got skipped.
finding.key_insight: Skipped entries cluster: 11 of 14 were two-claim summaries. The digest is not too long, it is under-split.
finding.evidence: 28 entries across 4 issues. 14 skipped on re-read. Failure tags: two-claim summary 11, no number where the headline had one 6, setup restated 5.
finding.next_step: Check whether the two-claim entries share a source type.

finding.summary: Ranked the failure modes and confirmed one dominates.
finding.key_insight: Two-claim summaries are 40% of entries and 79% of skips — every other mode is noise next to it.
finding.evidence: Ranked: two-claim 11/14 skips, dropped number 6, restated setup 5, missing disagreement 3. Long-read sources produce two-claim entries at 3x the rate of posts.
finding.next_step: Derive rules from the entries that were NOT skipped.

finding.summary: Drafted seven candidate rules from the entries that survived re-reading.
finding.key_insight: Four of the seven drafts restate one another — the rule set wants to be about splitting, not about length.
finding.evidence: Drafted 7. Pairwise check found 4 overlaps (three of them variants of 'one claim per entry'). 3 rules are independent and each is checkable from a single entry.
finding.next_step: Collapse the overlaps and re-check each rule against a skipped entry.

finding.summary: Collapsed to four rules, each checkable by reading one entry.
finding.key_insight: The 200-word cap is not a rule, it is a symptom of the split rule being unstated — drop the cap and keep the split.
finding.evidence: Final four: one claim per entry; lead with the disagreement; carry the headline's number; no restated setup. Each applied to all 14 skipped entries without needing a second rule to decide.
finding.next_step: Re-edit a real past digest against the four rules.

finding.summary: Re-edited the oldest of the four digests against the rule set.
finding.key_insight: The split rule turned 7 entries into 11 and the issue got SHORTER to read — the cap was fighting the edit, not enforcing it.
finding.evidence: 7 entries → 11. Word count 1,340 → 1,190. Every change traces to exactly one rule: split 4, disagreement-first 3, restored number 2, cut restated setup 5.
finding.next_step: Check the rules against an issue that was already considered good.

finding.summary: Applied the rules to a digest that had NOT been flagged, as a control.
finding.key_insight: Three of four rules changed nothing on the good issue — the rule set describes what the good entries were already doing, so it is a rule set and not a taste.
finding.evidence: Control issue: 9 entries, 2 changes (both restored numbers). Split and disagreement-first fired zero times, which is the result that makes the set credible rather than merely agreeable.
finding.next_step: Rules stand. Publish the set and re-read next week's issue against it.
